text: Bicol on blue alert as Super Typhoon Rosal enters PAR By Connie Calipay LEGAZPI CITY Bicol's Regional Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council RDRRMC placed the region under blue alert on Tuesday as Super Typhoon Rosal international name Champi entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility PAR at about 10:40 a m In Memorandum 60 series of 2026 RDRRMC Chairperson and Office of Civil Defense OCD Bicol Director Bernardo Fortes Jr directed regional response agencies and local disaster risk reduction and management councils to intensify preparations and closely monitor the weather disturbance's potential effects Under the directive concerned agencies must activate their Emergency Operations Centers EOCs around the clock ensure the readiness of response teams and assets and implement contingency plans based on anticipated hazards Response clusters led by various agencies have also been activated including the Department of Health DOH the Department of Social Welfare and Development DSWD for food and non-food items camp coordination and camp management and protection of internally displaced persons the Department of Information and Communications Technology DICT for emergency telecommunications the Philippine National Police PNP for law and order the Department of Education DepEd for education and the OCD for early recovery Provincial city and municipal disaster risk reduction and management councils were likewise instructed to hold pre-disaster risk assessment meetings activate their incident management teams and prepare evacuation centers and resources for possible emergency operations Fortes also directed them to advise residents in flood landslide and lahar-prone areas to prepare for possible evacuation Coastal communities vulnerable to storm surges were urged to remain alert and heed local advisories The memorandum also called for the immediate dissemination of weather bulletins and advisories to barangay disaster risk reduction and management committees and residents as well as the prompt reporting of incidents to the RDRRMC Operations Center Response agencies must ensure the availability of personnel and equipment for possible deployment test communication systems with higher-level operations centers and barangay disaster response teams and keep emergency hotlines updated on official websites and social media platforms In its bulletin on Tuesday the Philippine Atmospheric Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration PAGASA raised Wind Signal No 1 over parts of Northern Luzon including Batanes the eastern portion of the Babuyan Islands including Babuyan Camiguin and Didicas Islands the eastern portion of mainland Cagayan the northeastern portion of Isabela and the northeastern portion of Catanduanes Meanwhile DSWD-Bicol Director Norman Laurio said he was overseeing preparedness resource monitoring and coordination to ensure timely assistance for affected Bicolano families The regional social welfare office has prepositioned 410,158 family food packs FFPs 22,931 non-food items NFIs and 14,137 ready-to-eat food RTEF boxes in regional and local government unit warehouses to ensure timely assistance to affected families PNA Infographic courtesy of DSWD-Bicol

text: LILOAN CEBU CITY TAKE STEPS TOWARDS FLOOD MITIGATION ALONG COTCOT RIVER Mayor Aljew Frasco met with Cebu City Mayor Nestor Archival during a courtesy call at the Cebu City Mayor's Office to discuss possible solutions to address flooding that affects communities in Liloan and Cebu City particularly those along Cotcot River Since water in Cotcot River passes through Cambinucot and flows downstream toward Cotcot Bridge in Liloan monitoring water levels in this area is essential to provide an earlier warning of possible flooding During the meeting Mayor Aljew Frasco proposed the installation of an Early Warning System at Cambinucot Bridge to monitor rising water levels and alert residents of potential flooding Through this proposed system authorities can detect rising water levels earlier giving residents and concerned agencies more time to prepare and take precautionary measures before floodwaters reach downstream communities The two mayors also discussed the possibility of establishing a water catchment facility along the boundary of Cebu City and Liloan to help manage water flow and reduce flood risks The Municipality of Liloan extends its gratitude to Mayor Nestor Archival for welcoming Mayor Aljew and for the productive discussion toward strengthening flood preparedness and public safety

text: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources DENR Region 7 says Thursday Nov 13 2025 that massive tree cutting including multiple environmental violations at the Monterrazas de Cebu hillside development is uncovered during a probe launched amid reports of flooding and soil movement in the area triggered by Typhoon Tino In a radio interview Assistant Regional Director for Technical Services Eddie Llanedo said the investigation team found that more than 700 trees were cut within the 140 hectare property which is a serious breach of forestry and environmental laws During the Oct 2022 tree inventory there were 745 trees within the property of Monterazza The total property is 140 hectares Right now we found out that out of 745 only 11 were accounted for so meaning there was a violation of section 77 of Presidential Decree 705 or the Forestry Code of the Philippines Marita Moaje Photo from Monterrazas de Cebu Facebook page

text: As extreme weather severe flooding and crippling traffic continue to impact Metro Manila it becomes clear that single-purpose infrastructure is no longer enough We need multi-functional climate-resilient solutions designed for long-term survival In 1989 Arch Felino Jun Palafox Jr proposed a bold vision to complete the C 10 regional loop a tunnel interconnecting Bataan and Cavite Designed as a bridge and multi-tier underwater megastructure this concept serves a dual purpose 1 Transport and Connectivity Inspired by global best practices it links Central Luzon and Calabarzon directly-accommodating trains buses cars active mobility and utilities while bypassing the heavily congested roads of Metro Manila 2 Flood Management and Coastal Protection Similar to Malaysia's SMART Tunnel the infrastructure doubles as a massive flood control spillway during severe typhoons while acting as a natural wave breaker against storm surges By decentralizing Metro Manila and investing in dual-purpose infrastructure we can build a connected climate-resilient Philippines that protects both lives and livelihoods The best time to act was 37 years ago the second best time is today Pro Deo Patria et Terra PALAFOX

text: Laguna de Bay the largest lake in the Philippines is facing serious environmental challenges as pollution sediment accumulation and rapid urban development continue to place pressure on its ecosystem In August 2025 Biñan City Representative Walfredo Arman Dimaguila Jr warned that the lake could eventually become the country's largest septic tank if its deteriorating condition is not addressed His statement highlighted concerns about untreated wastewater industrial pollutants accumulated sediments and recurring flooding affecting communities surrounding the lake Covering approximately 900 square kilometers Laguna de Bay plays an important role in fisheries livelihoods water supply and flood regulation across Laguna Rizal and parts of Metro Manila However the lawmaker's description was a warning about environmental deterioration rather than a literal assessment of the lake's water quality Scientific assessments have identified several interconnected threats to Laguna de Bay including nutrient pollution siltation and eutrophication a process in which excessive nutrients stimulate algal growth and can contribute to oxygen depletion Wastewater from households industrial activities agricultural runoff and improper waste disposal can introduce organic matter nutrients microorganisms and other contaminants into the lake and its tributaries According to historical monitoring information from the Laguna Lake Development Authority LLDA domestic sources have contributed substantially to the lake's organic pollution load Excessive nutrients can encourage algal blooms while the decomposition of organic matter may reduce dissolved oxygen concentrations potentially harming fish and other aquatic organisms Sediment accumulation can also affect aquatic habitats and water movement although the extent to which it reduces floodwater storage requires updated measurements and hydrological assessment These environmental pressures are particularly concerning because many lakeshore communities depend on the lake for food income and other essential services In October 2026 Laguna lawmakers renewed calls for coordinated flood management through House Resolution No 906 which seeks an integrated approach involving updated lake surveys targeted dredging watershed rehabilitation erosion control and technical evaluation of flood mitigation infrastructure However scientists and environmental planners emphasize that dredging alone cannot solve water pollution especially when untreated wastewater and other contaminants continue entering the lake Effective rehabilitation requires improved sewerage and wastewater treatment stricter enforcement of environmental regulations responsible industrial waste management restoration of surrounding watersheds and continuous scientific monitoring Large-scale dredging proposals must also undergo careful environmental and engineering evaluation to determine their potential benefits costs and ecological impacts Protecting Laguna de Bay is not simply about preventing floods or removing accumulated sediments It is about safeguarding an essential freshwater ecosystem supporting fishing communities protecting public health and ensuring that future generations can continue to benefit from one of the Philippines most important natural resources Science Campaigner James Relativo in a Viber message The group said the protest was organized to call on regional leaders to take stronger action against the worsening pollution crisis in Southeast Asia It was held near Mactan Newtown the venue hosting the summit which brings together heads of state and government officials for the 48th ASEAN Summit 2026 In a press statement Greenpeace said the activists urged ASEAN leaders to end the plastic and waste crisis hold polluting corporations accountable and move the region away from the fossil fuel dependence driving climate harm The organization also stressed that authorities should listen to the concerns raised during the protest saying communities across Southeast Asia are already suffering from environmental issues such as landfill prioritize policies that reduce plastic production phase out single-use plastics strengthen waste prevention measures hold polluters accountable and support a shift toward reuse systems Meanwhile the text: SPAIN FOUR DEAD FOLLOWING STORM ADAM VALENCIA AND ALICANTE WITH RAINFALL TOTALS REACHING 700 mm The torrential rains of the last few days have resulted in extraordinary rainfall records across various parts of the Valencian region One of the most striking figures comes from Forna in the Marina Alta area where more than 700 l/m2 were recorded At least four people have died-one in Catalonia and three in the Valencian Community-following the passage of the storm Adam The storm hit Valencia and Alicante particularly hard bringing extraordinary rainfall with accumulations exceeding 700 l/m2 The situation is now beginning to improve and stay-at-home orders have been lifted in most of the affected municipalities The fatalities include a woman in Cabrera de Mar Barcelona who was swept away by a flash flood a victim in Sagunto Valencia whose body was recovered after she went missing while swimming with her partner at Corinto beach and two individuals in the town of Oliva Valencia In the latter case emergency services discovered a woman with limited mobility-who lived alone-on the ground floor of her home while the other victim was a man who suffered a fatal heart attack In the province of Alicante the Provincial Fire Consortium-deployed 15 units-focused its rescue efforts on the towns of Pego Els Poblets and El Verger Operations included both direct rescues and the pumping out of floodwater to reach residents trapped in affected areas José Luis Mas the mayor of Els Poblets Alicante described the town as being turned upside down noting that nearly half of the 900 residents in the town center were affected when the Girona River overflowed its banks He added however that fortunately there have been no fatalities or serious injuries In the Balearic Islands heavy rainfall has resulted in significant precipitation totals over the last 24 hours with 83.4 l/m2 recorded in Ibiza and 75.9 l/m2 Of the ten locations in Spain with the highest accumulated rainfall over the past 24 hours four are in the Balearic Islands Ibiza Es Codolar Lluc and Sant Elm The two precipitation maps one for the DANA of October 2024 and the other for the current event These two extraordinary events each with a different rainfall distribution have been documented thanks to data collected by hundreds of weather stations These maps are more than just images filled with colors and rainfall totals They represent information that helps better understand the territory study extreme weather events and preserve a meteorological record that will prove invaluable in the future

text: BAHA AT PAGGUHO NG LUPA NAITALA SA ARAKAN DAHIL SA SAMA NG PANAHON BABAE MISSING MATAPOS INANOD Nakaranas ng malakas na pag-ulan ang bayan ng Arakan Cotabato kagabi dahil sa Intertropical Convergence Zone o ITCZ na nagdulot ng ilang insidente ng pagbaha pagguho ng lupa at pagkasira ng mga imprastraktura batay sa situational report ng Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office o MDRRMO nitong Biyernes ng gabi Oktubre 9 Kabilang sa mga iniuulat ang pagka-anod ng isang bahay sa Sitio Mamag Barangay Allab kung saan may paunang ulat ding isang taong posibleng tinangay ng baha Hindi pa nakukumpirma ang pagkakakilanlan at kalagayan ng sinasabing nawawalang tao gayundin ang lawak ng pinsala Iniulat din na naanod ang isang box culvert sa Brgy Allab Sa Barangay Tumanding tinangay naman ng baha ang isang motorsiklo ngunit ligtas umano ang drayber Pansamantalang itinigil kagabi ang paghahanap sa motorsiklo dahil sa patuloy na malakas na ulan at hindi ligtas na kondisyon Samantala namonitor ang pagtaas ng tubig sa Tinanan Bridge sa Barangay Doroluman May nahulog ding linya ng kable sa kalsada malapit sa tulay na iniulat na inalis upang hindi na humarang sa mga motorista Sa Pormon Road sa Barangay Salasang nananatiling madadaanan ang kalsada ngunit may naobserbahang bahagyang pagguho ng lupa sa paakyat na bahagi Pinapayuhan ang mga motorista na mag-ingat dahil sa posibilidad ng karagdagang pagguho Makikita naman sa mga larawan na ito ang isinasagawang clearing operation ng mga BPAT members ABANTEROS at mga Barangay Officials sa tulay sa Sitio Valencia Sto Niño matapos ang malakas na flashflood Courtesy Ky C Sairf

text: Governor Azanza Nag-Isyu Ng Direktiba Sa Paghahanda Laban Sa Bagyong Champi Naglabas ng Opisyal na Memorandum No 236 Series 2026 ang Pamahalaang Panlalawigan ng Catanduanes sa pamamagitan ni Governor Patrick Alain T Azanza nitong Oktubre 19 2026 upang ipag-utos ang pagsasagawa ng mga kaukulang paghahanda at pag-iingat laban sa banta ng Bagyong Champi Ipinadala ang nasabing direktiba sa lahat ng alkalde mga chairperson at miyembro ng Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council MDRRMC mga response agency at iba pang sangkot na tanggapan sa buong lalawigan Ayon sa huling ulat ng panahon ganap na 3:00 ng madaling araw ang sentro ng Bagyong Champi ay tinatayang nasa 1,720 kilometro Silangan ng Timog-Silangang Luzon sa labas ng Philippine Area of Responsibility PAR Taglay nito ang lakas ng hangin na pumapalo sa 175 km/h at pagbugsong umaabot sa 215 km/h habang kumikilos pakanluran-hilagang-kanluran sa bilis na 25 km/h Inaasahang magdadala ng malalakas na pag-ulan ang bagyo sa buong lalawigan Kaugnay nito inatasan ang lahat ng kinauukulang ahensya na ipatupad ang mga sumusunod na hakbang sa paghahanda Mga Paaralan Inatasan ang mga pinuno ng pampubliko at pampribadong paaralan na muling ipaalala ang DEPED MEMO 22 S 2024 at DEPED MEMO No 014 S 2026 tungkol sa pagsususpinde ng klase at mga alituntunin sa pagpapatuloy ng pag-aaral sa panahon ng emergency MDRRMCs Inutusang bantayan nang maigi ang epekto ng sama ng panahon i-activate ang 24/7 Emergency Operations Center EOC at agad na maglabas ng weather bulletins sa mga Barangay DRRMC Ipinag-utos din ang pagsubmit ng mga lagdaang situational report sa PDRRMC EOC at pag-update ng EOC hotlines Klase at Trabaho Ang lokalisadong pagsususpinde ng trabaho at klase ay nakasalalay sa desisyon ng mga LCEs o MDRRMC Chairperson Mga Paghahanda sa Komunidad Inatasan ang pagputol sa mga sanga ng puno malapit sa linya ng kuryente at bahay paglilinis ng mga kanal at waterways upang maiwasan ang pagbaha at ang pagpapakalat ng babala sa mga naninirahan sa tabi ng ilog kabundukan at mababang lugar Evacuation at Prepositioning Pinahihintulutan ang mga LGU na magpatupad ng paglikas kung kinakailangan at inatasan silang mag-preposition na ng pagkain non-food items at rescue teams sa mga estratehikong lugar Pangingisda at Karagatan Makikipag-ugnayan ang mga MDRRMC sa Philippine Coast Guard PCG para sa pagpapatupad ng No Sailing Policy kapag naglabas ng Gale Warning Advisory ang PAGASA Kesiguruduhan ng Publiko Pinapayuhan ang publiko na iwasan ang hindi importanteng pagbibiyahe lalo na sa mga daang madalas bahain o malapit sa ilog at manatiling nakatutok sa opisyal na babala mula sa DOST-PAGASA at OCD Maaaring ipadala ng MDRRMO/Cs at mga response agency ang kanilang situwal na ulat sa PDRRMC EOC sa pamamagitan ng hotline number na 0912-670-7777 o sa opisyal na PDRRMO-Catanduanes Facebook Page

text: Rosal PH PAGHAHANDA SA POSIBLENG PAGBAHA AT LANDSLIDE IPINAG-UTOS SA MGA LGU SA CATANDUANES Inatasan ang mga lokal na pamahalaan sa Catanduanes na paigtingin ang mga hakbang laban sa posibleng pagbaha at landslide kasunod ng pagtaas sa Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No 1 sa hilagang-silangang bahagi ng lalawigan dahil sa Super Typhoon Rosal Saklaw ng Signal No 1 ang mga bayan ng Pandan Bagamanoc Panganiban Viga at Gigmoto Sa Memorandum No 236 Series of 2026 na inilabas ni Governor Patrick Alain T Azanza nitong Oktubre 19 iniutos ang paglilinis ng mga kanal at daluyan ng tubig paghahanda ng mga relief goods at rescue team at posibleng paglikas ng mga residenteng nasa mga lugar na nanganganib sa sakuna Inatasan din ang mga municipal disaster risk reduction and management council na mahigpit na subaybayan ang lagay ng panahon paandarin ang kanilang mga emergency operations center nang 24 oras at agad na ipakalat ang mga weather bulletin at babala sa mga barangay Kailangang iulat ang mga insidente sa Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council Emergency Operations Center sa pamamagitan ng pirmadong situational report at tiyaking napapanahon ang mga hotline na nakapaskil sa mga pampublikong plataporma Nasa pagpapasya ng mga lokal na punong ehekutibo at mga tagapangulo ng local disaster risk reduction and management council ang suspensiyon ng trabaho at klase sa kanilang nasasakupan Inatasan din ang mga paaralang pampubliko at pribado na sundin ang mga umiiral na direktiba ng Department of Education hinggil sa suspensiyon ng klase at pagpapatuloy ng pagkatuto sa panahon ng emergency Kabilang pa sa mga hakbang ang pagputol sa mga sanga ng punong malapit sa linya ng kuryente gusali at kabahayan gayundin ang paghahanda sa paglikas ng mga residenteng nasa mga lugar na madaling bahain at magkaroon ng landslide Samantala inatasan ang mga kinauukulang ahensiya na makipag-ugnayan sa Philippine Coast Guard para sa posibleng lokal na pagbabawal sa paglalayag kapag naglabas ang PAGASA ng gale warning Kailangang bantayan din ang kondisyon ng dagat posibleng storm surge at high tide sa mga komunidad sa baybayin Pinayuhan ang publiko na iwasan ang hindi kailangang pagbiyahe lalo na sa mga kalsadang madaling bahain at malapit sa mga ilog at sumubaybay sa mga opisyal na abiso ng PAGASA at Office of Civil Defense via Juriz Dela Rosa Radyo Pilipinas Radyo Publiko Integrated State Media Catanduanes

text: HALOS PHP 100 MILYONG FLOOD CONTROL PROJECT SA CALAMBA NAIWANG TIWANGWANG AT NANGANGANIB BUMAGSAK KAHIT PHP 49 MILYON NA ANG NAI-DISBURSE NG DPWH CALAMBA CITY LAGUNA Pormal nang dinala sa Office of the Ombudsman ang umano'y kuwestiyonableng implementasyon ng halos PHP 100 milyong pisong flood-control project sa kahabaan ng San Juan River sa Barangay Sampiruhan matapos madiskubreng nakatagilid at nanganganib bumagsak ang retaining wall nito kahit mahigit siyam na buwan na ang lumipas mula sa itinakdang petsa ng pagtatapos Batay sa reklamong inihain ng mga residente sa pangunguna ni Calamba City Councilor Christian Niño Lajara nagkakahalaga ng kabuuang PHP 93,972,467.00 ang naturang proyekto sa ilalim ng kontratista nitong Power K Construction Supply and Services Ayon sa mga opisyal na talaan dapat sana ay natapos ang konstruksyon mula Pebrero 14 2025 hanggang Enero 6 2026 Subalit sa aktwal na ocular inspection sa lugar tinatayang wala pa sa 10 porsiyento ang totoong natatapos sa lupa habang tanging mga bakal na nakatulos sa pampang ang pumipigil sa pader upang hindi ito tuluyang gumuho sa ilog Ang nakagugulat pa rito nakatala sa opisyal na database ng Department of Public Works and Highways DPWH na 75.47 percent complete na umano ang proyekto at nakapaglabas na ang pamahalaan ng mahigit PHP 49 milyong piso para rito Binigyang-diin ni Konsehal Lajara na bukod sa matinding agwat ng datos sa papel laban sa aktwal na kalagayan sa ilog buhay at kabuhayan ng mga magsasaka at residente sa paligid ang inilalagay sa matinding panganib tuwing sasapit ang tag-ulan dahil nananatili ang pagbaha sa lugar sa kabila ng dambuhalang pondo Muling binuhay ng insidenteng ito ang panawagan para sa masusing imbestigasyon sa bilyun-bilyong pisong inilaan sa mga flood control project sa buong Laguna sa gitna ng tila pananahimik ng ilang lokal na opisyal sa lalawigan ukol sa kalidad at tunay na katayuan ng mga pinondohang imprastraktura

text: HINDI LAHAT NG DREDGING NAKIKITA SA BALITA ALAM MO BA ANG GINAGAWA SA LIKOD NITO Marami ang nag-aakalang puro barko at pagkuha lamang ng buhangin ang ginagawa ng ISLA VERDE MINING AND DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION IVMDC Pero alam ba ninyo na bahagi rin ng kanilang ginagawa ang pagsisikap na mapalalim ang Abra River at maalis ang mga nakaharang na buhangin sa daluyan nito Dahil sa mga naipong buhangin na humahadlang sa pagpasok ng mga barko sa ilog patuloy ang mga pagsisikap na maibalik ang maayos na daloy ng tubig at mapanatiling bukas ang daluyan ng Abra River Sa mga nakaraang araw ng walang tigil na pag-ulan mahalagang mapansin ang naging kalagayan ng mga barangay sa tabi ng Abra River Sa kabila ng malalakas na pag-ulan hindi nakaranas ng pagbaha ang mga naturang barangay sa panahong tinutukoy Hindi man ito palaging nababalita mahalagang maunawaan ng ating komunidad ang mga gawaing isinasagawa sa ilog at ang layuning mapabuti ang daluyan nito Alam ba ninyo na ang ISLA VERDE MINING AND DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION ay nagsasagawa ng pagtulong sa pagpapalalim ng Abra River nang walang sinisingil na bayad sa gobyerno para sa gawaing ito Layunin nitong makatulong sa maayos na daloy ng tubig at mabawasan ang panganib na kinakaharap ng mga komunidad sa tabi ng ilog lalo na tuwing malakas at tuloy-tuloy ang pag-ulan Para sa mga pamilyang nakatira sa mga lugar na posibleng maapektuhan ng baha mahalaga ang bawat hakbang na makatutulong sa kanilang kaligtasan at kapanatagan ng isip IBA ANG NAKIKITA SA LABAS MAY MGA GAWAING HINDI NAKIKITA NG LAHAT Patuloy nating alamin unawain at pag-usapan ang mga proyektong may kinalaman sa ating ilog kalikasan at kaligtasan ng komunidad Isla Verde Mining IVMDC Abra River Dredging Operations Para Sa Komunidad Ilocos Sur One Ilocos Sur bantaykalikasan Malinis Na Kalikasan Ligtas Na Kinabukasan

text: LOOK AB PolSci 3B attends the traditional Pamuhat for the DPWH Flood Control Mitigation Project As part of the class POSCI 63 Political Socialization and Culture Prof Hermie P Pava the CMU Vice President for Administration invited PolSci 3B to attend and witness the traditional ritual called Pamuhat for DPWH's Flood Control Mitigation Project The ritual was attended by various offices of the University as well as representatives from the DPWH and the engineers As Political Culture students we not only witnessed the ritual but also the rich culture and tradition of Bukidnon which shape its distinct identity We also came to the realization that rituals like Pamuhat do not only represent the past but also indicate our future It is very important to preserve the rich culture that we have even in this era of modernization as this is a crucial part of our identity-something without which we cannot truly live as a society The entire AB PolSci 3B would like to extend our deepest and sincerest gratitude to our beloved instructor Mr Pava for allowing us to experience and witness this wonderful occasion It is indeed true that the best learning also transpires outside the four corners of our classroom because our knowledge has been deepened through this practical experience We are truly looking forward to more experiences like this in the future and to making more memories together as a class both blocks A and B while deepening our knowledge and understanding not only of the subject but of the reality as a whole Hawkvelahap AB Pol Sci3B Pol Culture

text: Why Blame PBBM for a Flood-Control Mess He Exposed The devastating Habagat floods of August 2026 have understandably caused anger and frustration Filipinos have every right to demand accountability But why blame President Ferdinand R Marcos Jr for a flood-control problem that his administration itself exposed During his Fourth State of the Nation Address on July 28 2025 President Marcos publicly revealed the alarming irregularities in flood-control projects and ordered their inspection and verification Investigations subsequently uncovered projects allegedly reported as completed but found to be nonexistent defective improperly located or below required standards-some dating back to 2016 during the previous administration The issue is not simply how much money was appropriated but whether Filipinos actually received the infrastructure they paid for Billions of pesos cannot simply disappear while projects exist only on paper If public officials or contractors misused government funds they must be held accountable under Article XI Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution which declares that public office is a public trust and under Republic Act No 3019 the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act Of course the Marcos administration must also be held accountable for projects undertaken during its own term No administration should be above scrutiny But it is unfair to automatically blame the incumbent president for every consequence of decades of inadequate or allegedly anomalous infrastructure A problem inherited for years cannot be corrected overnight Investigating questionable projects identifying those responsible recovering public funds prosecuting offenders and rebuilding failed infrastructure take time If corruption occurred under the previous administration those responsible should answer for it If corruption occurred under the present administration those responsible should likewise face the law The question should therefore not be Why blame PBBM Nor should it be Why blame Duterte The real question is Who received the people's money who failed to deliver what was promised and who should be held accountable Let the evidence answer-not political loyalty The Filipino people deserve flood-control projects that actually exist actually work and actually protect them
